what: Zebra makes the barcode scanners, rugged handheld computers, label printers and tracking software used to move goods through warehouses, shops and hospitals.
customers: Retailers, parcel carriers, warehouse operators, manufacturers and hospitals, buying hardware in fleets and replacing it on a cycle.
money: barcode and RFID printers, supplies and location tracking
handheld computers, scanners, tablets and software
moat: Devices embedded in a customer's warehouse software and staff training, which makes switching brands a project rather than a purchase, plus a reseller network that reaches small operators.
risks: Revenue fell from $5.8B to $4.6B in 2023 when customers stopped replacing devices, and has not regained the peak
Purchases come in fleets, so a customer postponing a refresh removes a quarter's revenue at once
Most manufacturing is in Asia, which exposes the cost base to tariffs
opportunities: Free cash flow of $988M against a $14.7B market value, and analysts see about 32% upside
The installed base is ageing and devices bought in the 2021 e-commerce boom are due for replacement
RFID tagging is spreading from clothing retail into groceries and logistics, which sells both tags and readers
watch: Whether device replacement orders return, and the growth of the RFID business.
